conflicts.issue: Future Land Use Map Change from Medium-Density Residential to Commercial (Item 23)
conflicts.summary: Council divided 2-5 over whether to override Planning Commission and staff opposition to reclassify residential property on the Future Land Use Map to commercial.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve commercial designation for economic development and neighborhood stability
side_a_arguments: Approving the applicant's commercial request offers an opportunity to bring jobs, business activity, and economic stability to the area.
conflicts.side_b_position: Deny the commercial amendment and concur with staff and Planning Commission
side_b_arguments: Planning Commission and staff recommended against the commercial reclassification.
Neighborhood opposition highlighted nearby convenience-store crime, an adjacent stream behind the parcel, senior residents, and notice concerns.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to approve the land use plan amendment failed 2-5, with Clement and Stith voting yes.

conflicts.issue: Item 34: Historic Landmark Designation — Withall House (LDO 6-1)
conflicts.summary: Following City Attorney guidance on a motion to approve so Council could defeat the request per staff and Historic Preservation Commission recommendations, Council voted down the designation due to non-historic vinyl siding and replaced windows.

conflicts.issue: Consent Item 37 and Alcohol Licensing Impact on Neighborhoods
conflicts.summary: Council Member Howard Clement III cast the sole dissenting vote on Consent Item 37 (6-1) and raised broader objections during Item 8 over community harms from alcohol outlets.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve Consent Item 37 as part of routine licensing/consent business
side_a_arguments: License renewals and routine applications met statutory requirements, with fees capped by state law at $25 unless amended by the General Assembly.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose Consent Item 37 due to neighborhood alcohol-related harms
side_b_arguments: Too many unfortunate incidents have occurred in neighborhoods where alcohol connections have been abused.
conflicts.resolution: Consent Item 37 passed 6-1, with Council Member Howard Clement III recorded as voting No.

conflicts.issue: City $2 Million Financing/Liability Structure in Heritage Square and Golden Belt Deal Points
conflicts.summary: Council divided 6-1 over whether the City should accept a $2 million upfront funding/loan liability in non-binding deal points for the $135 million Heritage Square and Golden Belt revitalization project.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the non-binding deal points including the $2M city funding commitment
side_a_arguments: Investing $2 million alongside the developer's private risk in a $135 million historic revitalization project is a sound business decision benefiting the community.
Upfront streetscape design funds are needed early and staff can defray costs toward the final development agreement as done with West Village.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose putting the city on the line of liability for $2 million; prefer property tax incentive adjustment
side_b_arguments: Deal points quickly solidify into contract terms, and the city should not carry $2M in liability if project projections do not hold.
The city should increase the property tax rebate share (e.g., from 80% to 85%) rather than loan-financing $2M upfront.
conflicts.resolution: Motion to execute the non-binding deal points passed 6-1, with Thomas Stith III voting no.

conflicts.issue: Economic Development Incentive Job Thresholds and Geographic Targeting (Items 18 and 28)
conflicts.summary: Council split 6-1 on both amendments lowering the city's business incentive job threshold and an accompanying incentive contract for a bioscience firm relocating to Durham.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve lower job-creation thresholds and award the bioscience incentive contract
side_a_arguments: Updated downtown boundaries, definitions, and job thresholds enable Durham to attract high-wage young firms such as the relocating bioscience company ($75,000–$90,000 salaries).
conflicts.side_b_position: Retain higher job-creation thresholds and target incentive dollars to designated community development areas
side_b_arguments: While welcoming the company and supporting updated downtown boundaries, lowering the job threshold weakens incentive standards.
City incentive funds should be focused on targeted community development areas rather than lowered thresholds.
conflicts.resolution: Both Item 18 (policy changes) and Item 28 (bioscience incentive contract) passed 6-1 with Diane Catotti voting no.

conflicts.issue: 2007 Legislative Program Outline — Local Option Transportation Tax, Impact Fees, and Prepared Food Tax ('Other' Items 1, 6, and 8)
conflicts.summary: During consideration of the 2007 Legislative Program Outline, Council Member Thomas Stith III objected to three local revenue and tax proposals in the 'Other' category—a local option transportation tax (Item 1), homeowner impact fees (Item 6), and a prepared food/meals tax (Item 8)—while the remaining six Council members supported including them in the City's legislative package.
conflicts.side_a_position: Include the local option transportation tax, impact fees, and prepared food tax in the 2007 Legislative Program Outline.
side_a_arguments: Maintains the full legislative package to seek General Assembly authority for local revenue options, with clarification that Item 8 applies to prepared food and statements noted by a speaker that Council Member Diane Catotti indicated some proceeds would support workforce initiatives.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose including Other Items 1 (transportation tax), 6 (impact fees), and 8 (prepared food tax) in the legislative program.
side_b_arguments: Opposed raising the local option tax for transportation.
Argued impact fees would be passed on to homeowners.
Criticized the food/prepared food tax as a regressive tax.
conflicts.resolution: Council voted 7-0 on the overall 2007 Legislative Program Outline while recording Thomas Stith III as voting Nay on 'Other' Items 1, 6, and 8 (passing those three items 6-1).

conflicts.issue: Item 23: Future Land Use Map Amendment (Medium-Density Residential to Commercial)

conflicts.issue: Renewal and Oversight of Beer and Wine Licenses (Item 17)
conflicts.summary: Council voted 6-1 on reconsideration to approve beer and wine licenses, with Howard Clement III dissenting over neighborhood alcohol impacts and requesting police call reports by address for renewals.
conflicts.side_a_position: Approve the listed beer and wine license applications and renewals
side_a_arguments: Proceeded with standard approval of the August 2006–January 2007 beer and wine license list.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose routine approval without police-activity reporting by address for renewals
side_b_arguments: Renewals should be accompanied by police activity reports per address to monitor problem locations.
Excessive alcohol consumption harms student populations and fragile neighborhoods.
conflicts.resolution: Passed 6-1 on reconsideration with Howard Clement III voting no; staff agreed to check with the Police Department regarding address-level police reports.

conflicts.issue: Extension of Temporary Taxicab Fuel Surcharge Ordinance (Item 27)
conflicts.summary: Council Member Thomas Stith III registered a dissenting vote on extending the temporary taxicab fuel surcharge ordinance.
conflicts.side_a_position: Extend the temporary taxicab rate ordinance authorizing a fuel surcharge
side_a_arguments: Approved alongside consent items to continue the temporary fuel surcharge authority.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose extending the taxicab fuel surcharge
side_b_arguments: Continuing concern over the surcharge's impact on riders.
conflicts.resolution: Item 27 passed 6-1 with Thomas Stith III recorded as voting no.

side_a_arguments: Supported advancing the city's 2007 legislative agenda package ahead of the meeting with the legislative delegation.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose Resolutions 5, 9, and 11 (referencing tax/food tax concerns)
side_b_arguments: Registered opposition to Resolutions 5, 9, and 11 during discussion noting food tax concerns.
conflicts.resolution: Resolutions 5, 9, and 11 passed 5-1 with Thomas Stith III voting no (Diane Catotti absent/excused), and the remaining legislative agenda passed 6-0.

conflicts.issue: City Funding for a Private School (Item 15)
conflicts.summary: Council divided 5-1 on Item 15, concerning city funds for a private school, with Council Member Eugene Brown registering a formal 'no' vote in opposition while five colleagues supported moving and adopting the item via the Consent Agenda.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support approving Item 15 on the Consent Agenda after prior staff question resolution
side_a_arguments: Staff had already answered Council members' prior questions on the item
No need to hold Item 15 for separate General Business Agenda debate

side_b_arguments: Objected substantively to allocating city funds to a private school
Initially favored keeping the item on the General Business Agenda to register opposition before agreeing to consent placement once his 'no' vote was recorded

conflicts.issue: City Council Resolution on DA Mike Nifong Resignation / Support for Judicial Suspension (Item 61)
conflicts.summary: Council members disagreed on whether the Durham City Council should adopt a formal position regarding District Attorney Mike Nifong following state bar disciplinary proceedings and reports of Chief Superior Court Judge Orlando Hudson's planned suspension order.
conflicts.side_a_position: Support Council taking a formal stand calling for Nifong's departure or endorsing Judge Hudson's removal action
side_a_arguments: Council should show leadership alongside Governor Mike Easley, the Attorney General, and local judges to help the community move forward.
Following the State Bar findings of dishonesty and misrepresentation, expressing Council support for Judge Hudson's planned suspension helps rebuild community trust.
conflicts.side_b_position: Oppose City Council taking a formal resolution or vote on the District Attorney
side_b_arguments: The judicial and State Bar process was underway and Council was already conducting its own police investigation.
The District Attorney is a countywide elected office outside City Council's jurisdiction and better left to county bodies and the Superior Court.
conflicts.resolution: Council Member Eugene Brown's modified motion to express support for Judge Hudson's planned suspension action died for lack of a second; no vote was taken.

conflicts.issue: Independent Third-Party Investigation into Police Handling of the Duke Lacrosse Case
conflicts.summary: Following the City Manager and Police Chief's May 11 internal report on the Duke Lacrosse investigation, Council members differed on whether to commission an independent third-party review and what scope, cost, and purpose it would serve.
conflicts.side_a_position: Commission an independent, non-partisan third-party investigation into the Police Department's handling of the case
side_a_arguments: The May 11 internal report did not go far enough and no city-issued report will be free of charges of whitewash.
An impartial outside review is needed to rebuild public confidence in the Police Department, administration, and City Council.
conflicts.side_b_position: Question the cost, timeframe, and added value of an additional investigation before committing
side_b_arguments: Need clear answers on cost, timeframe, and what new information an extra investigation would yield.
Questions about officer conduct may already be answered by comments from the Attorney General and special prosecutors.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote taken; Council members planned to submit written questions and continue deliberation at Thursday's work session.

conflicts.issue: Scheduling of 'Sanctuary City' Immigration Resolution Discussion and Member Robocalls
conflicts.summary: Council Member Thomas Stith III contended that Durham's 2003 resolution conflicted with police practices and state/federal law and claimed the City Manager had assured him it would appear on the September 17 agenda, whereas Mayor Bill Bell stated Council had agreed to handle the issue at Thursday's work session and criticized Stith's automated robocalls.
conflicts.side_a_position: Address the 'sanctuary city' designation and align police policy and practice immediately
side_a_arguments: Congressional Research Service designated Durham a sanctuary city, potentially jeopardizing federal funds in pending federal legislation.
Current policy conflicts with state law and reported police practice regarding status inquiries during criminal investigations.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defer policy discussion to the Thursday work session as agreed when setting the agenda
side_b_arguments: Council settled the agenda to allow the administration and police department time to prepare a resolution for the Thursday work session rather than a regular Monday voting session.
Automated robocalls telling residents Durham was a haven for illegal immigrants and that the item would be heard Monday misled the public.
conflicts.resolution: No formal vote was taken; the matter remained scheduled for discussion at the Thursday work session.

conflicts.issue: Specificity and Funding Accountability in Administration's State of the City Response (Item 36)
conflicts.summary: Council members challenged City Manager Patrick Baker over whether the administration's initial report on neighborhood revitalization, street lighting, and violent crime hotspots contained specific funding commitments and accountable execution plans.
conflicts.side_a_position: Demand concrete funding allocations, dedicated staff accountability, and specific actionable proposals rather than preliminary reports
side_a_arguments: Without putting dedicated dollars behind revitalization plans, proposals remain ineffective.
Specific street-level remedies and clear staff accountability are needed after Council neighborhood tours so complaints do not feel ignored.
conflicts.side_b_position: Defend the report as an initial response backed by nearly $500,000 in proposed budget additions
side_b_arguments: The proposed budget already adds $100,000–$150,000 for street lighting, over $200,000 for code enforcement/lot cleanup, over $200,000 for police hotspots, six new officers, and additional street repair crews.
This preliminary presentation will be followed by a holistic plan with measurable goals and objectives.
conflicts.resolution: Informational presentation concluded without a formal vote; City Manager committed to returning with measurable goals and budget-backed details.

meetings.title: Special City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 28, 2007 Special City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden with six Council members present (Mayor Bill Bell absent), the Council held a three-hour quasi-judicial hearing on Case M07-01, a Major Special Use Permit for Reclamation Station Recycling Center at 1404 East Geer Street in an Industrial Light (IL) district. Proponents—including the applicant, the Inter-Neighborhood Council, and retired Water Management Director Terry Rolan—testified that the grease-trap waste and used fryer oil recycling facility would help restaurants comply with city sewer Fats, Oils, and Grease (FOG) rules and reduce long-distance hauling, while committing to spill containment and odor controls. Northeast Central Durham residents and District 1 neighborhood leaders strongly opposed the permit, citing proximity to homes, truck traffic, odor concerns, limited outreach to PAC 1, and conflict with the 2006 RKG revitalization plan. After adding binding conditions restricting materials to grease-trap waste and used fryer oil, limiting storage to two mobile liquid tanks, setting operating hours to 7 a.m.-6 p.m., and mandating revocation upon violation, the Council unanimously approved the permit 6-0. No split or contested votes occurred.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff Michael Stock outlined UDO Section 3.9 findings required for a recycling center in the IL district. Applicants, the Inter-Neighborhood Council, and retired Water Management Director Terry Rolan testified that the facility would process grease-trap waste and fryer oil under DENR Solid Waste oversight, reducing sewer blockages and long-haul transport. District 1 residents and Northeast Central Durham leaders opposed the site over odors, truck traffic, lack of PAC 1 outreach, and revitalization goals; after amending conditions to cap storage at two mobile liquid tanks, restrict hours to 7 a.m.-6 p.m., and specify automatic revocation upon noncompliance, Council voted 6-0 to adopt the permit order.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 19, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden, the Council voted 6-0 to excuse Mayor Bill Bell and proceeded with six seated members present. Following proclamations for Arbor Day and poverty/AIDS awareness and a brief water-supply update projecting temporary Teer Quarry piping within weeks, the Council unanimously approved the Manager's priority agenda adjustments (6-0) and received the Police Department's third-quarter crime report showing four-year lows in larcenies alongside a four-year high in burglaries. On the Consent Agenda, Council approved all items unanimously (6-0) except Item 1F (voluntary annexation petition), which passed 5-0 with 1 abstention: Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, and Diane Catotti voted Aye, while Thomas Stith III abstained on advice of the City Attorney due to a potential conflict of interest. Concluding a contested public hearing, the Council unanimously approved the Garrett Road rezoning and development plan (6-0) after the applicant added committed elements for a Garrett Road sidewalk, $1,000 per student ($29,000) to Durham Public Schools, and $10,000 toward relocating the historic Clifton and Lee Garrett house.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Excusal of Mayor Bell, and Proclamations
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the meeting to order, six Council members answered roll call, and Council voted 6-0 to excuse Mayor Bill Bell. Proclamations were presented for Arbor Day (December 1, 2007) and global poverty and AIDS awareness, alongside Council comments on Art Walk turnout and upcoming property tax revaluation and revenue-neutral rate disclosures.

agenda_items.title: City Manager's Priority Items and Water Supply Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager requested adding Item 1H (Jordan at Southpoint voluntary annexation public hearing, FY 2007-14) and hearing Item 44 (third-quarter police crime report) right after the consent agenda; Council approved both priority items 6-0. Staff also updated Council on engineering temporary pipes to draw from Teer Quarry within weeks and expanding Jordan Lake access beyond 2 million gallons per day via Cary.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (with Abstention by Thomas Stith III on Item 1F)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council considered Consent Agenda Items 1-46 (excluding general business items 24 and 44), covering voluntary annexation petitions, board appointments, Woodcomb Street closing (SC07-01), utility extension agreements, Downtown Durham Inc. contract, 2007 GO bond referendum certification (Item 43), and water conservation code amendments (Item 46). Council Member Thomas Stith III declared an abstention on Item 1F due to a potential conflict on advice of the City Attorney; the consent agenda passed 6-0 overall (5-0-1 on Item 1F).
agenda_items.vote_summary: Passed 6-0 (5-0-1 on Item 1F with Stith abstaining)

agenda_items.title: Item 44: Police Department Third Quarter Crime Report (Jan-Sep 2007)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police leadership presented the third-quarter 2007 year-to-date crime report. Property crimes and larcenies were at four-year lows, and murders, rapes, robberies, and total index crimes were second lowest in four years, whereas burglaries reached a four-year high and aggravated assaults, violent crimes, and motor vehicle thefts were the second highest in four years.

agenda_items.title: Garrett Road Rezoning and Development Plan
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Environmental speakers urged deferring the rezoning to protect downstream water resources amid the drought, while the applicant and Garrett Farms HOA representatives defended negotiated commitments including a 250-foot setback for two-story structures along Garrett Road, US 15-501 road improvements, and LEED/water-conservation design features. The applicant added three committed elements (#32-34): constructing a sidewalk along west Garrett Road to Oak Creek shopping center, contributing $1,000 per student for 29 additional students to Durham Public Schools, and contributing $10,000 toward relocating the Clifton and Lee Garrett house; Council approved the rezoning 6-0.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the November 5, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council presented a proclamation for Home Care and Hospice Month and adopted a memorial resolution honoring former Mayor Harry Edwin Rodenhizer Jr. (7-0). During the water-supply report, staff projected approximately 144 days of supply including Nello Teer Quarry access and reported 495 water-violation reports, 194 warnings, and 6 formal violation notices, with service termination pending for one repeat offender. The Council unanimously voted (7-0) to continue a transitional zoning public hearing to November 19 so the sitting Council could conclude it prior to seating newly elected members, and unanimously approved initial zonings for Obedience to the Word (Z07-16A, Item 24, 7-0) and Bungalow Avenue (Z07-04A, Item 25, 7-0). Following public scrutiny from Victoria Peterson on Item 17 (Employment Training Grant), Workforce Development staff reported serving over 100 trainees—roughly 25 percent from Northeast Central Durham—and agreed to supply detailed demographic and placement data before Council approved Item 17 unanimously (7-0). No split or contested votes occurred.

agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. with all seven Council members present, presented a Home Care and Hospice Month proclamation to Ron Thompson, and presented a memorial resolution honoring former two-term Mayor Harry Edwin Rodenhizer Jr. (1979-1981 and 1991-1993) to his widow Doris Faye Taylor Rodenhizer and family. Council later formally adopted the supplemental resolution (Item 33) by a 7-0 vote.

agenda_items.title: Council Remarks and Water Supply Enforcement Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council recognized Durham's Finance and Budget staff for their 19th consecutive Distinguished Budget Presentation award and celebrated the Durham Station groundbreaking. In the drought update, staff reported 144 days of water supply when counting Teer Quarry access, previewed proposed fine and reconnection-fee revisions, and noted 495 violation reports, 194 warning notices, 6 violation notices, and one impending service shutoff for a repeat offender.

agenda_items.title: Continuation of Public Hearing to November 19, 2007

meetings.executive_summary: At the August 20, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council honored retiring Water Management Director Anthony Terrell 'Terry' Rolan after 33 years of service and proclaimed August 27, 2007 as Durham Striders Track and Field Day. Council Member Mike Woodard also noted the opening of a JobLink facility at Antioch Baptist Church and the passing of Duke University and Research Triangle Park pioneer Dr. Marcus Hobbs. In legislative business, Council unanimously adopted a General Obligation Bond Order (7-0) for street repairs and sidewalks—clarifying that 'very poor' and 'poor' rated streets would be prioritized while dirt-street paving remains petition-driven—with the understanding that staff would present street lists and property-tax impact estimates at a future work session. No split or contested votes occurred.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Terry Rolan Retirement Proclamation, and Durham Striders Track and Field Day
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with all seven Council members present and honored retiring Water Management Director Terry Rolan for 33 years of city service and water-planning leadership. meetings.executive_summary: At the August 6, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council opened with ceremonial recognitions including the introduction of North Carolina Central University's new 10th Chancellor, the 2007–2008 Durham Youth Council, a proclamation for CARA, National Conference of Black Mayors scholarship recipients, and neighborhood crime prevention awards. Following approval of the consent agenda (7-0, excluding pulled Items 21 and 25), Police Chief Steve Chalmers presented the second quarter 2007 crime report, noting four-year lows in property crimes and larcenies alongside a four-year high in burglaries and ongoing officer recruitment. During public hearings, the Council unanimously approved (7-0) a development site plan along Austin Avenue and NC 54, Comprehensive Plan amendment A07-05 for 8.5 acres on Andrew Avenue, the Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report amendments, and two street closings (SC07-02 and SC07-03). After resolving pulled consent Items 21 (Durham Arts Council contract) and 25 (City Manager right-of-entry agreement authority) by unanimous 7-0 votes, the meeting adjourned at 9:40 p.m. with no split votes or formal disagreements.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Ceremonial Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. and the Clerk confirmed all seven Council members were present. Mayor Pro Tem Cora Cole-McFadden introduced North Carolina Central University's new 10th Chancellor, who spoke on education as an engine of opportunity. Council also recognized the 2007–2008 Durham Youth Council, issued a proclamation for HIV/AIDS organization CARA, honored National Conference of Black Mayors scholarship winners, recognized Durham Police Department crime prevention and neighborhood watch milestones, and noted the 50th anniversary of the June 1957 Durham sit-in.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda (Items 13–20, 23–24, 28–34)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk read consent agenda headings covering Xerox equipment leases, a COPS reimbursement resolution, annual reports for the Durham Open Space and Trails Commission and Historic Preservation Commission, street acceptances, the May 2007 business loan report, employment and training grant amendment #13397, Parkwood Fire Department contract renewal, community sign panels, MPO GIS contracts, and water reclamation SCADA systems. Items 21 and 25 were pulled for separate consideration, and the remaining consent items were approved unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 37: Durham Police Department Second Quarter 2007 Crime Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Police Chief Steve Chalmers, Major Lee Russ, and Crime Analyst Supervisor Jason Schiess presented the January–June 2007 crime report. Data showed property crimes and larcenies at a four-year low and index crimes (murders, rapes, and robberies) at their second lowest total in four years, while aggravated assaults and motor vehicle thefts were the second highest and burglaries hit a four-year high. Chief Chalmers also reported 489 of 500 sworn officer positions filled, with 32 rookies expected in the August 13 academy class alongside 12 newly budgeted officers.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Austin Avenue and NC 54 Site Plan Sidewalk Requirement
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council discussed sidewalk frontage along Austin Avenue adjacent to the old two-story school building on a County development site plan. Staff confirmed that city ordinance requires sidewalk construction along the portion of frontage being developed, while future developers of the remaining site would be required to complete the rest of the sidewalk. After closing the public hearing, Council approved the item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 42: Comprehensive Plan Amendment A07-05 (Andrew Avenue)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a request by Tony M. Tate Landscape Architecture to change the Comprehensive Plan land use designation on 8.5 acres on the north side of Andrew Avenue from commercial to low-medium density residential for a better land-use transition. Both the Planning Commission (12-0 on May 8, 2007) and the Durham Board of County Commissioners (unanimously on July 23) had previously recommended or voted for approval. agenda_items.title: Evaluation and Assessment Report (EAR) Plan Amendments (A07-07)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented the required Comprehensive Plan Evaluation and Assessment Report proposing two land use amendments and one text change, plus ratification of two modifications made by the Board of County Commissioners on July 23. Staff answered a Council question clarifying that designating downtown as a business district authorizes related city actions as reviewed by the City Attorney's Office. Following the public hearing with no outside speakers, Council approved the item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 44: Street Closing SC07-02 (Two Unnamed Alleys off Corporation and Gilbert/Guillot Streets)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented a request by Union Missionary Baptist Church to permanently close two unnamed alley segments of 125.45 linear feet and 170.04 linear feet, confirming the request met all North Carolina statutory and City Code requirements for closing public right-of-way. agenda_items.discussion_summary: Item 21, funding the establishment of a Durham Chapter of the Arts and Business Council via contract with the Durham Arts Council, had been pulled by Victoria Peterson, who was not present when called. meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the June 18, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Council opened with ceremonial recognitions including honoring the commissioning of the CCB Plaza bronze bull sculpture ('Major'), declaring July 18, 2007 as Ride/Bike to Work Day, and presenting a memorial resolution honoring William Jesse Kennedy III. Council approved priority agenda modifications from the City Manager (7-0, moving municipal candidate filing fees to consent and flagging Item 59 contingency) and the City Attorney (housekeeping Item 60 for the Duke Lacrosse investigatory committee). Later, Council unanimously adopted Item 60 (7-0) establishing procedures for calling a special meeting to consider subpoenas and witness swearing-in, while a sharp governance disagreement emerged on Item 61 over District Attorney Mike Nifong: Thomas Stith III and Eugene Brown favored Council taking a formal stand—initially calling for Nifong's resignation and then modified by Brown to express support for Chief Superior Court Judge Orlando Hudson's planned suspension order—while Bill Bell and Howard Clement III opposed Council taking a position on a countywide elected prosecutor, and Brown's modified motion died for lack of a second (no roll-call vote). Finally, following citizen remarks on local and African American hiring in downtown projects, the Council unanimously approved Item 22 (7-0) before adjourning at 10:28 p.m.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Proclamations, and Memorial Resolution for William Jesse Kennedy III
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. and Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance. Ceremonial items included recognizing the commissioning of the bronze bull sculpture 'Major' at CCB Plaza honoring George Watts Hill, proclaiming July 18, 2007 as Ride/Bike to Work Day, and presenting a memorial resolution honoring community leader and NC Mutual executive William Jesse Kennedy III, read by Council Member Thomas Stith III.

agenda_items.title: Council Requests for Supplemental Item 61 (DA Mike Nifong Resignation) and Priority Items
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Thomas Stith III requested adding Item 61 for Council to join Governor Mike Easley, Judge Hudson, and the Attorney General in calling for District Attorney Mike Nifong's immediate resignation, and Council Member Eugene Brown concurred. City Manager Patrick Baker moved Item 2 (municipal candidate filing fees) back to the consent agenda and flagged Supplemental Item 59 (City Council contingency), which passed 7-0, while the City Attorney introduced Supplemental Item 60 for Duke Lacrosse investigatory committee housekeeping.

agenda_items.title: Item 60: Duke Lacrosse Investigatory Committee Housekeeping and Special Meeting Procedures
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council addressed procedures for a special meeting to decide on issuing subpoenas and administering oaths via the City Clerk. Council Member Howard Clement III requested stipulating that four affirmative votes (a majority of the full seven-member Council, not three of four in a special meeting) be required to issue a subpoena. The City Attorney advised that Council rules and law already require four members for a quorum and four affirmative votes for any official action, and Council adopted the resolution unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Item 61: Proposed Position on District Attorney Mike Nifong and Judge Orlando Hudson's Actions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell cited a News & Observer report that Chief Superior Court Judge Orlando Hudson planned to suspend DA Mike Nifong and appoint a special prosecutor, stating he would vote against calling for Nifong's resignation while the city's own police review proceeded. Council Member Eugene Brown modified the motion to express Council support for Judge Hudson's planned removal action, while Council Member Howard Clement III argued the DA is a countywide official outside the City Council's jurisdiction. After discussion, the motion died for lack of a second.

agenda_items.title: Item 22 (Pulled Consent): Durham Arts Council and Workforce Diversity on Downtown Projects
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Victoria Peterson spoke on Items 22 and 23 regarding streetscape and Skanska projects downtown, asking what safeguards ensure local Durham citizens and African American laborers obtain construction jobs. City staff clarified that city ordinance permits monitoring SDBE and minority business participation—with breakdowns by African American and other minority businesses—rather than individual contractor hiring, and promised to provide SDBE compliance reports. Council then approved Item 22 unanimously.

disagreements.summary: Council members disagreed on whether the Durham City Council should adopt a formal position regarding District Attorney Mike Nifong following state bar disciplinary proceedings and reports of Chief Superior Court Judge Orlando Hudson's planned suspension order.
disagreements.side_a_position: Support Council taking a formal stand calling for Nifong's departure or endorsing Judge Hudson's removal action
side_a_arguments: Council should show leadership alongside Governor Mike Easley, the Attorney General, and local judges to help the community move forward.

disagreements.resolution: Council Member Eugene Brown's modified motion to express support for Judge Hudson's planned suspension action died for lack of a second; no vote was taken.

Mayor Bell proclaimed June 5, 2007 as Make-A-Wish Day in Durham, and Council Member Thomas Stith III presented resolutions honoring local Tuskegee Airmen and Congressional Gold Medal recipients Dr. Stuart Fulbright (first dean of NCCU's business school) and William McDonald (retired NCCU physical plant administrator). Council members kept announcements brief due to the lengthy budget public-hearing agenda.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Items (Item 36 Placement, Item 41 Annexation Withdrawal, Police Chief Finalists)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Patrick Baker moved Item 36 (initial response to the Mayor's State of the City address) to the General Business Agenda, reported that Ingram Estates withdrew its voluntary annexation petition from Item 41 Section B while remaining annexations proceeded, and announced a June 5 meet-and-greet with finalists for the next Durham Police Chief. Council approved the priority items unanimously 6-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Rural Residential Land Use Designation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a public hearing on a proposed rural residential land use designation. With no members of the public wishing to speak, the public hearing was closed and Council approved the item unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Citizen Comment: DATA Transit Evening, Weekend, and Holiday Service
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resident Mr. Graham asked Council to add evening, weekend, and holiday DATA bus service to New Hope Commons and TTA connections. Mayor Bell referred the request to transportation director Mark Ahrendsen for consideration during upcoming budget deliberations.

agenda_items.title: Item 36: City Manager's Initial Response to Mayor's State of the City Address
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Patrick Baker and staff presented an initial report addressing downtown Business Improvement District recommendations, targeted neighborhood revitalization with PAC engagement, street lighting repairs and tree trimming, and violent crime reduction via expanded 90-day hotspot initiatives and six additional police officers. Council members including Mayor Bill Bell and Howard Clement III criticized the preliminary nature of the report and demanded dedicated dollars, assigned accountability, and concrete proposals. Baker responded that the proposed budget includes nearly $500,000 in added funding for street lighting, code enforcement, street repair crews, and police hotspots, with detailed measurable objectives to follow.

votes.notes: Mover and seconder were not named in the transcript digest; Clerk/Mayor announced passage by 7 votes.
votes.discussion_detail: Approval of rural residential land use designation following uncontested public hearing.

disagreements.issue: Specificity and Funding Accountability in Administration's State of the City Response (Item 36)
disagreements.summary: Council members challenged City Manager Patrick Baker over whether the administration's initial report on neighborhood revitalization, street lighting, and violent crime hotspots contained specific funding commitments and accountable execution plans.
disagreements.side_a_position: Demand concrete funding allocations, dedicated staff accountability, and specific actionable proposals rather than preliminary reports
side_a_arguments: Without putting dedicated dollars behind revitalization plans, proposals remain ineffective.
Specific street-level remedies and clear staff accountability are needed after Council neighborhood tours so complaints do not feel ignored.
disagreements.side_b_position: Defend the report as an initial response backed by nearly $500,000 in proposed budget additions
side_b_arguments: The proposed budget already adds $100,000–$150,000 for street lighting, over $200,000 for code enforcement/lot cleanup, over $200,000 for police hotspots, six new officers, and additional street repair crews.
This preliminary presentation will be followed by a holistic plan with measurable goals and objectives.
disagreements.resolution: Informational presentation concluded without a formal vote; City Manager committed to returning with measurable goals and budget-backed details.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 21, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council proclaimed May 20–26, 2007 as National Public Works Week and recognized the Durham Youth Council. Council referred Item 9 (purchasing contract approval thresholds) back to the administration (7-0) and approved the consent agenda (7-0, excluding pulled Items 23 and 36). City Manager Patrick Baker presented the preliminary FY 2007–2008 Budget and FY 2008–2013 Capital Improvement Plan emphasizing crime reduction, core municipal services, and 2005 bond execution, while Council unanimously approved a UDO text amendment (7-0) and later passed pulled Items 23 (Carolina Theatre renovations) and 36 (Contract ST-224 downtown improvements) 7-0 despite Council Member Thomas Stith III raising concerns about a $3 million (27%) cost overrun and project delays. The meeting closed with an extended debate (no formal vote, deferred to Thursday's work session) over the May 11 Duke Lacrosse internal report: Mayor Bill Bell, Mike Woodard, and Cora Cole-McFadden favored an independent third-party review of the Police Department's conduct while Bell and Diane Catotti opposed any Council resolution calling for DA Mike Nifong's resignation, and Catotti questioned the cost, timeframe, and necessity of an additional investigation.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and National Public Works Week Proclamation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with all seven Council members present. Mayor Bell proclaimed May 20–26, 2007 as National Public Works Week and presented the proclamation to Public Works Director Kathryn Kalb following a demonstration of the department's new pothole repair equipment. Council also recognized the Durham Youth Council ahead of its November youth conference in Durham.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Priority Item (Refer Item 9 Purchasing Thresholds) and Consent Agenda
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Patrick Baker asked Council to refer Item 9 (purchasing contract approval thresholds) back to the administration for further discussion, which Council approved 7-0. Council then approved the consent agenda 7-0 with the exception of Items 23 and 36, covering board appointments, the March 2007 bid report, general obligation bond reimbursement, water/sewer extensions, a Cricket Communications water-tank lease, and Triangle Area water monitoring. Council Member Howard Clement III also asked the Manager for an overdue update on the shared $2M+ DOJ Raleigh-Durham anti-gang grant.

agenda_items.title: Item 30: Presentation of Proposed FY 2007–2008 Budget and FY 2008–2013 CIP
agenda_items.discussion_summary: City Manager Patrick Baker presented the preliminary FY 2007–2008 budget and FY 2008–2013 Capital Improvement Plan. He noted the proposal incorporated input from January–February Council retreats, a February public hearing, a record seven Coffees with Council, PAC units, and advisory boards, focusing on crime, core municipal functions, and implementing the 2005 bond program.

agenda_items.title: Item 32: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council held a public hearing on a Unified Development Ordinance text amendment. No members of the audience signed up or spoke, and Council approved the text amendment unanimously.

agenda_items.title: Items 23 and 36 (Pulled Consent): Carolina Theatre Renovations and Contract ST-224 Downtown Improvements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Items 23 and 36 to urge adding a local workforce component ensuring legal Durham residents and African American workers are hired by subcontractors on Carolina Theatre and downtown projects. Council Member Thomas Stith III criticized the $3 million (27%) cost overrun and schedule delays on Contract ST-224 downtown improvements and asked what monitoring mechanisms protect capital and bond projects; staff attributed the overrun to material cost escalation and standard weather-delay clauses. Council approved both Item 23 and Item 36 unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Added Item: Review of City Manager/Police Chief Duke Lacrosse Investigation Report
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated the May 11 internal report by the City Manager and Police Chief on the Duke Lacrosse investigation. Mayor Bill Bell, Mike Woodard, and Cora Cole-McFadden argued that an independent, non-partisan third-party investigation of the Police Department's role is necessary to restore public confidence and answer accusations of whitewash, while Bell and Diane Catotti opposed any Council resolution demanding DA Mike Nifong's resignation. Catotti also questioned the cost, timeframe, and necessity of an extra investigation, and Thomas Stith III noted he would bring detailed questions to Thursday's work session.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 7, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, Council recognized local elementary winners of the Drinking Water Week poster contest, proclaimed Bimbe Cultural Arts Festival Week, heard the Durham Youth Council year-in-review, and welcomed a Sister Cities delegation from Kostroma, Russia. The key policy division centered on authorizing the City Manager to execute non-binding deal points with Woodlake Avenue Partners and Edgemont Realty LLC for the $135 million Heritage Square and Golden Belt neighborhood revitalization project: in a 6-1 split vote, Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, and Diane Catotti voted Aye to advance the deal points and $2 million city infrastructure/streetscape commitment as a sound community investment, while Thomas Stith III voted Nay, objecting to city liability on the $2 million funding piece and advocating a property tax incentive adjustment (such as 85% instead of 80%) instead. Council subsequently approved four pulled consent items (Items 12, 13, 15, and 24) by unanimous 7-0 votes after public queries on HUD Continuum/Katrina funds, Walmart grants, and senior housing workforce requirements, and Howard Clement III asked for a proration plan before voting to accept the shared DOJ anti-gang grant.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Proclamations, Durham Youth Council, and Sister Cities Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with all seven Council members present and Council Member Howard Clement III leading the Pledge of Allegiance. Council presented proclamations for Drinking Water Week (honoring elementary poster contest winners who swept the statewide AWWA contest), Bimbe Cultural Arts Festival Week (May 11–20), and AIDS orphans awareness. Durham Youth Council President Angelica Powell gave a year-in-review report, and Sister Cities President Richard Hill introduced a visiting delegation from Kostroma, Russia.

agenda_items.title: Heritage Square and Golden Belt Non-Binding Deal Points (Woodlake Avenue Partners / Edgemont Realty LLC)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council debated authorizing the City Manager to execute non-binding deal points with Woodlake Avenue Partners and Edgemont Realty LLC for the $135 million Heritage Square and Golden Belt revitalization project. Council Member Thomas Stith III praised staff for shifting certain risks to the developer but objected to the city assuming liability for a $2 million funding/loan component, proposing an 85% property tax incentive share instead. Council Member Eugene Brown argued the $2 million investment in a $135 million revitalization project is a worthwhile business risk, and the motion passed 6-1 with Stith voting no.

agenda_items.title: Item 12 (Pulled Consent): Grant Project Ordinance for HUD Continuum / Co-op Grant Fund
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 12 regarding the HUD grant project ordinance. Council moved, seconded, and unanimously approved the ordinance 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 13 (Pulled Consent): Hurricane Katrina HUD Fair Housing Grant Funding
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 13 to ask why specific outside groups were receiving Hurricane Katrina fair housing funds and whether they partnered with local nonprofits on job training. Staff explained that HUD structured the grant for affected states such as Mississippi to re-establish fair housing for displaced or returning residents. Council approved the item unanimously 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 15 (Pulled Consent): Walmart Safe Neighborhood / Community Grant Funds
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 15 to ask if the $2,500 and $1,000 Walmart grants to the Police Department could be directed to Triangle Citizens Rebuilding Communities for fiber-optic certification training for ex-offenders. City Manager Patrick Baker agreed to ask the Police Chief and follow up, and Council approved the item 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Item 24 (Pulled Consent): Senior Housing Funding Proposals on City-Owned Land (Chapel Hill Rd. & Whitcomb St.)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Victoria Peterson pulled Item 24 (funding proposals for senior housing on 2.3 acres of city-owned land at Chapel Hill Road and Whitcomb Street) to ask whether a local workforce development component was included. City Manager Baker noted that page 4 of the packet reflected Self-Help's commitment to comply with Chapter 26 SDBE provisions, and Council approved the item 7-0. Afterward, Council Member Howard Clement III requested a division/proration plan for the shared Raleigh-Durham DOJ anti-gang grant before Council votes to accept funds.

disagreements.issue: City $2 Million Financing/Liability Structure in Heritage Square and Golden Belt Deal Points
disagreements.summary: Council divided 6-1 over whether the City should accept a $2 million upfront funding/loan liability in non-binding deal points for the $135 million Heritage Square and Golden Belt revitalization project.
disagreements.side_a_position: Approve the non-binding deal points including the $2M city funding commitment
side_a_arguments: Investing $2 million alongside the developer's private risk in a $135 million historic revitalization project is a sound business decision benefiting the community.
Upfront streetscape design funds are needed early and staff can defray costs toward the final development agreement as done with West Village.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose putting the city on the line of liability for $2 million; prefer property tax incentive adjustment
side_b_arguments: Deal points quickly solidify into contract terms, and the city should not carry $2M in liability if project projections do not hold.
The city should increase the property tax rebate share (e.g., from 80% to 85%) rather than loan-financing $2M upfront.
disagreements.resolution: Motion to execute the non-binding deal points passed 6-1, with Thomas Stith III voting no.

meetings.executive_summary: At the April 16, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present, the Council observed a moment of silence for the Virginia Tech tragedy, received a recognition from Durham Public Schools Vice Chair Steve Schewel, presented a Fair Housing proclamation to the Durham Housing Authority, honored North Carolina Central University championship athletic teams, and presented a resolution and Key to the City to outgoing NCCU Chancellor Dr. James Ammons. City Manager Patrick Baker referred Item 25 (UDO animated/motion signs) back to the administration and flagged Item 34 (Capital Broadcasting Company economic development incentive contract) for public hearing continuance. During the land-use public hearings, Council split 2-5 to defeat Item 23—a future land use plan amendment from medium-density residential to commercial—against staff and Planning Commission recommendations: Howard Clement III and Thomas Stith III voted Aye arguing commercial zoning would bring jobs and economic stability, while Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, and Diane Catotti voted Nay following opposition citing neighborhood crime, an adjacent stream, and notice concerns (with a voting-machine reset interruption occurring on companion Item 24). meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the February 19, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell, the Council unanimously excused Council Member Diane Catotti's absence (6-0) and celebrated local athletic achievements including a junior track-and-field champion and the undefeated Rogers-Herr Lady Rams basketball team. meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven Council members present, the February 5, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting opened with ceremonial presentations, including the 2006 Durham Jaycees Civic Award presented to the City of Durham and General Services staff member Laurie Blake Reed for hosting the Jaycees' haunted house at Durham Bulls Athletic Park, a youth mentoring proclamation tied to Mayor Bell's State of the City mentoring alliance initiative, a memorial resolution presented by Council Member Howard Clement III to the family of a late Hillside High School alumnus (transcribed in ASR as John Wilson Embers/Ebits), and a proclamation declaring February 5–9, 2007 as Human Relations Week. Council announcements highlighted the 40th anniversary of the Eno River Association, African-American Achievement Day at Shepard Magnet Middle School, Boy Scout Troop 440, the Nelson Mandela exhibit at the American Tobacco Campus, and the second annual Durham Police Department Block Captain Workshop at the old Hillandale School. The middle portion of the meeting—including the East End Connector public hearing referenced in opening remarks—was omitted by digest truncation before the recorded FY 2007–2008 budget input public hearing, where speakers urged Council to shift funding from downtown subsidies toward neighborhood stabilization, affordable housing, $50 million over five years for the Fayetteville Street Plan to prevent displacement in Hayti/Hayes Town, and General Fund support for core Community Development functions rather than CDBG, HOME, or ESG funds. On the lone recorded vote in the available digest, Council voted unanimously 7-0 to close the FY 2007–2008 budget public hearing and receive public comments, followed by staff confirming a Fayetteville Street sidewalk repair contract would return after a second bidding round; no split or contested votes appeared in the available digest.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Silent Meditation, Pledge of Allegiance, and Roll Call
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the regular City Council meeting to order at 7:10 p.m. on Monday, February 5, 2007, and led a moment of silent meditation. Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and the City Clerk called the roll with all seven Council members present.

agenda_items.title: Ceremonial Presentations: Durham Jaycees Civic Award, Mentoring Proclamation, Memorial Resolution, and Human Relations Week
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Mike Woodard introduced Mark Greenspan, General Services staff member Laurie Blake Reed, and 2006 Durham Jaycees President Aaron Locklear, who presented the 2006 Durham Jaycees Civic Award to Reed and the City of Durham for hosting the Jaycees' haunted house at Durham Bulls Athletic Park for three consecutive years. Mayor Bill Bell read a youth mentoring proclamation referencing his State of the City mentoring alliance remarks, Council Member Howard Clement III presented a framed memorial resolution to the family of a late Hillside High School graduate (transcribed in ASR as John Wilson Embers/Ebits), and Bell joined Human Relations Executive Director Yvonne to proclaim February 5–9, 2007 as Human Relations Week.

agenda_items.title: Council Member Announcements and Community Recognitions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council remarks welcomed residents attending for the State of the City follow-up, the East End Connector public hearing, and the first FY 2007–2008 budget public hearing, while congratulating the Eno River Association on its 40th anniversary, Shepard Magnet Middle School, the Durham Chamber of Commerce, and Boy Scout Troop 440. Remarks also highlighted the Nelson Mandela lithograph exhibit at the American Tobacco Campus and commended Durham Police Department Officer Eric Hester and Kimberly Walker for hosting 135 block captains at the second annual Block Captain Workshop; subsequent business between 00:29:21 and 02:54:29 was omitted by digest truncation.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: FY 2007–2008 Budget Input and Neighborhood Investment Priorities
agenda_items.discussion_summary: During the public hearing on the FY 2007–2008 budget, speakers urged Council to reallocate $500,000 toward Habitat for Humanity homes, second mortgages for first-time homebuyers, volunteer minor home repairs for elderly and disabled residents, and special-needs housing. Larry Hester of the Fayetteville Street Planning Group requested $50 million over five years for the Fayetteville Street Plan and warned that downtown-focused subsidies and recent rezonings between NC 147 and Cornwallis/Juan Wallace Road risk displacing Hayti/Hayes Town residents, while Citizens Advisory Committee representative Mr. Clifton urged funding core code enforcement from the General Fund rather than CDBG, HOME, or ESG grants and West End resident David Anthony praised neighborhood investments.

agenda_items.title: Post-Hearing Follow-Up on Fayetteville Street Sidewalks and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Howard Clement III reminded residents that budget public input would continue through June 2007 and praised the Citizens Advisory Committee's work. Following a Council inquiry regarding Larry Hester's comments on promised Fayetteville Street sidewalks, staff explained that an initial bid round lacked sufficient bidders and that a contract from the second bidding round would come before Council within two to three cycles before Council adjourned.

votes.item_title: Close Public Hearing and Receive FY 2007–2008 Budget Public Comments
votes.notes: Mover and seconder not identified by name ('properly moved and seconded'); clerk opened and closed the vote and the chair announced 7-0 passage.
votes.discussion_detail: Closed the public hearing and formally received citizen comments on FY 2007–2008 budget priorities, housing affordability, Fayetteville Street corridor investment, and CDBG/HOME/ESG allocations.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the January 16, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting to order and presided through the opening and consent agenda with six members present in the absence of Mayor Bill Bell, who arrived later in the meeting prior to the concluding zoning and pulled items. The meeting opened with a youth mentoring proclamation praising Durham Companions and local mentors, tributes including recognition of the passing of former Durham County Commissioner Eleanor Spaulding, and an administrative update noting the selection of an independent vendor to review water lead testing and notification procedures ahead of a Lead Summit. Two split 5-1 votes occurred early in the meeting regarding Item 15 (city funds for a private school): on the procedural motion to move Item 15 to the consent agenda, the vote was recorded 5-1 (Ayes: Cora Cole-McFadden, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, Thomas Stith III, Mike Woodard; Nay: Eugene Brown, though Brown clarified verbally that he supported moving it to consent while maintaining his opposition to Item 15 itself), and on the final Consent Agenda adoption, the remaining consent items passed 6-0 while Item 15 passed 5-1 (Ayes: Cora Cole-McFadden, Diane Catotti, Howard Clement III, Thomas Stith III, Mike Woodard; Nay: Eugene Brown; Mayor Bill Bell absent). Following a truncated middle segment that began during Item 18 on surplus real estate disposal for affordable housing, all seven Council members—now joined by Mayor Bell—unanimously approved (7-0) Zoning Map Change 06-48 at 5601 Fayetteville Road, UDO Text Amendment TC06-12 on swimming pool fencing, UDO Text Amendment TC06-16 on RSM multi-family open space, and pulled Consent Items 8 (Criminal Justice Resource Center employment training subrecipient agreement) and 19 (2005 Bond playground design services).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Youth Mentoring Proclamation, and Community Tributes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: In Mayor Bill Bell's temporary absence, Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden called the meeting to order, led silent meditation, and had Council Member Howard Clement III lead the Pledge of Allegiance, with six Council members answering roll call. Cole-McFadden read a mentoring proclamation thanking Durham Companions and local mentors, and Council members offered community remarks including a tribute to the late Eleanor Spaulding, the first Black person and first woman to serve as a Durham County Commissioner (1974–1984).

agenda_items.title: Motion to Move Item 15 (City Funds for a Private School) to Consent Agenda and Water Lead Testing Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Because staff questions on Item 15 (city funds for a private school) and Item 18 had been answered, Council moved Item 15 to the Consent Agenda while keeping Item 18 on the General Business Agenda because a speaker had pulled it. Council Member Eugene Brown stated he wanted Item 15 left on the record as a negative vote in opposition to city funds for a private school while consenting to place it on the Consent Agenda; the machine vote recorded 5-1 and Brown clarified his intent with the Clerk, followed by a brief update that an independent vendor had been identified to review city water lead testing and notification processes ahead of a Thursday Lead Summit.

agenda_items.title: Consent Agenda Approval (Items 1–7, 9–11, 13–17, 21, 25; Items 8, 18, and 19 Pulled)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The Clerk read the Consent Agenda covering minutes, bid and business loan reports, a Fay Street closing public hearing schedule, major site plans (Madison Pointe/Glantu D06-352 and Lighthouse of Durham/Maple Court Apartments D06-475), water and sewer extension agreements, subrecipient agreements for Durham Crisis Response Center, Durham Affordable Housing Coalition, and Operation Breakthrough, Community Builders Inc. contract, Parrish Street retail incentives ($70,000 set-aside), South Carolina CDC Whitted/Whitcomb Street land redevelopment update, police operations/equipment funding up to $250,100, and Durham Central Park environmental restoration. Items 8, 18, and 19 were pulled for separate consideration, and the Consent Agenda passed 6-0 with Council Member Eugene Brown voting no on Item 15 (making Item 15 pass 5-1).

agenda_items.title: Criteria and Procedures for Disposing of Surplus Real Estate to Nonprofits for Affordable Housing
agenda_items.discussion_summary: On the General Business Agenda, Council opened Item 18 establishing criteria and procedures for disposing of surplus city real estate to qualifying nonprofit organizations for affordable housing. Speakers Jack Price and Nadine Lappell (on behalf of the Durham Housing Authority) began addressing Council before the middle portion of the transcript digest (00:39:46 to 02:37:47) was truncated.

agenda_items.title: Zoning Map Change: 5601 Fayetteville Road (06-48)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented Zoning Map Change 06-48 requested by Deborah Long and Ronald Kimman to rezone just under 1 acre at 5601 Fayetteville Road from RS-20 to Office and Institutional with a development plan prohibiting drive-through windows and restricting access to one-way in and one-way out. Dan Jewell spoke in support on behalf of the applicants and longtime property sellers, noting commercial surroundings and a Fayetteville Road median restricted driveway access, and Council approved the rezoning 7-0 (with Mayor Bill Bell now present and presiding).

agenda_items.title: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendment: Swimming Pool Fencing (TC06-12)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented UDO Text Amendment TC06-12, initiated by the Joint City-County Planning Committee and recommended 7-3 by the Planning Commission, codifying the Planning Director's interpretation that a swimming pool inside a completely fenced yard does not require a separate secondary enclosure and adjusting the installation compliance date to April 1. No members of the public spoke during the public hearing, and Council adopted the amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Unified Development Ordinance (UDO) Text Amendment: RSM Multi-Family Open Space Revision (TC06-16)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented UDO Text Amendment TC06-16, initiated by the Joint City-County Planning Committee and recommended 12-0 by the Planning Commission, extending open space requirements in the Suburban Residential Multi-family (RSM) district from townhome subdivisions to multi-family apartment projects. Following an open public hearing with no speakers, Council approved the text amendment 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Subrecipient Agreement with Durham County Criminal Justice Resource Center
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Pulled by speaker Victoria Peterson, who questioned spending $64,800 on 12 participants and urged employment commitments for city Project Strike participants, Item 8 funded a carpentry and employment training program at the Criminal Justice Resource Center. Staff member Larry Jarvis clarified the grant covers two cycles of 12 participants (24 total beneficiaries receiving ~$2,700 stipends), and Deputy Director Joe Iverson and Program Manager Robin Heath explained that target populations include Police Department STARS participants and unsupervised individuals released from prison, while welcoming Project Strike applicants before Council approved the agreement 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item: Design Services Agreement for Site Playgrounds (2005 Bond Projects)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up the final pulled consent item, Item 19, an agreement for design services for site playgrounds funded by 2005 Bond Projects. Following brief two-minute public comment, Council approved the agreement 7-0 and adjourned at 9:50 p.m.

meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven Council members present, the January 2, 2007 Regular City Council Meeting marked the City of Durham's first live internet broadcast via its redesigned website and opened with a moment of silent meditation honoring the National Day of Mourning, an excused absence vote (7-0) for Council Member Thomas Stith III, and Stith's request to form a citizens committee within 30 to 60 days to oversee a departmental performance audit. City Manager briefings addressed referring Contract ST-227 street improvements (Item 18) back to administration, downtown police staffing during a December 31 early morning homicide at 119 West Main Street, and heightened Council scrutiny over newspaper reports that the city failed to disclose 20 special water lead tests in seven homes, prompting Council members and Mayor Bell to seek written notification policies and an independent third-party review to restore public trust. Following a truncated middle segment, Council addressed a Walmart site plan clarification (explaining that floodplain-triggered revisions are strictly administrative) and held a contested 5-1-1 vote on a land use amendment (specific project title omitted in the truncated digest), which passed 5-1 with 1 abstention (Ayes: Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Thomas Stith III; Nay: Diane Catotti; Abstention: Bill Bell). Council subsequently voted unanimously 7-0 to adopt UDO Text Amendment TC06-19 repealing suburban-tier chain link fence restrictions and to approve initial city zoning map changes for Triangle Metro Center (06-2618), the Simcoe Property on Page Road, and the John Roch Property (06-6658).

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, National Day of Mourning Meditation, Roll Call, and Live Webcast Launch
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Following a brief technical delay setting up live internet streaming, Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order around 7:05 p.m. and all seven Council members answered roll call. Bell led a moment of silent meditation noting the National Day of Mourning, Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and Council Member Thomas Stith III welcomed online viewers to the city's first live internet broadcast on the redesigned durhamnc.gov website while congratulating Chuck Davis on his 70th birthday and 50-year dance career.

agenda_items.title: Citizens Performance Audit Committee Request and Excused Absence
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council Member Thomas Stith III asked the City Manager to place formation of a citizens committee to select a city department for a performance audit on the January 18 agenda so the effort could launch within 30 to 60 days. Stith also requested an excused absence for January 4, which Council approved 7-0.

agenda_items.title: City Manager Briefing: Item 18 Referral, Dec. 31 Downtown Homicide, and Water Lead Testing Review
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager asked Council to refer Consent Item 18 (Contract ST-227 street improvements) back to administration and briefed Council on the December 31 early morning homicide of Sherard Jamal McNair at 119 West Main Street, noting an arrest warrant had been issued and three officers (two supervisors and a beat officer) remained on downtown duty after supplemental patrols ended at 2 a.m. Council extensively questioned the City Manager regarding news reports that 20 special water lead tests from seven homes were not disclosed or reported to residents; while staff stated those voluntary pH-adjustment tests did not carry a statutory notification mandate prior to October 1, Mayor Bell and Council members stressed public trust, requested written notification policies, and called for an independent review (referencing EPA or DENR) before approving the manager's priority items/referral by voice vote and swearing in Rochelle Newton-Brown to the Durham Housing Authority.

agenda_items.title: Walmart Site Plan Clarification and Land Use Amendment Vote
agenda_items.discussion_summary: After a truncated middle segment (00:48:36 to 01:19:20), staff clarified for neighbors that Walmart's revised site plan—required to comply with newly mandated federal and state floodplain ordinance changes—was a purely administrative action with no Council discretion remaining after prior zoning approval. Council then voted on a land use amendment (specific item title omitted in the truncated digest) after a Council member disclosed his wife belonged to a supporting organization; the measure passed 5-1 with 1 abstention (Catotti voting no; Bell abstaining).

agenda_items.title: UDO Text Amendment: Chain Link Fencing Repeal (TC06-19)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented UDO Text Amendment TC06-19 repealing Section 9.9.2B restrictions on chain link fences in the suburban tier (which required vinyl coating and a top cap rail), noting homeowners were being cited because fencing installers failed to inform them of the rule. Initiated by the Joint City-County Planning Committee and recommended 13-1 by the Planning Commission on November 14, 2006, the repeal passed 7-0 after a public hearing with no speakers.

agenda_items.title: Initial Zoning Map Change: Triangle Metro Center (06-2618)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented initial city zoning for over 44 recently annexed acres north of Hopson/Hofstra Road and east and west of Davis Drive, applying the closest city designations (O&I-D, CC-D, IL, and RU-MD) to reflect county vested rights granted by the Board of Commissioners. Both staff and the Planning Commission recommended approval, and Council adopted the initial zoning 7-0 with no public speakers.

agenda_items.title: Initial Zoning Map Change: Simcoe Property (Page Road)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented translational initial city zoning (RR and IP) for over 32 recently annexed acres on the east side of Page Road south of Wind River Parkway and north of Smallwood Drive spanning former Durham County and Wake County (R-4) jurisdictions. Planning Commission found the interim zoning reasonable and in the public interest, Cara Lacey of the John R. McAdams Company spoke in support, and Council approved the map change 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Initial Zoning Map Change: John Roch Property (06-6658)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presented standard initial city zoning for the newly annexed John Roch property (06-6658) matching its prior unincorporated Durham County designations with no land use changes. Following a public hearing with no speakers, Council approved the item 7-0, heard announcements of the January 17 MLK Jr. joint celebration at First Presbyterian and Friday's budget retreat at the Museum of Life and Science, and adjourned at 8:26 p.m.
