meetings.title: Regular City Council Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: At the December 18, 2006 Durham Regular City Council Meeting presided over by Mayor Bill Bell with all seven members present (Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, Diane Catotti, and Thomas Stith III), Council presented a ceremonial resolution reaffirming the 2003 Bill of Rights Defense Resolution, approved the City Manager's priority items 7-0 (including referring the Police Department Long-Range Master Facility Plan back to administration and scheduling the Q3 2006 crime report), and heard consent agenda item notices before a truncated middle portion of the transcript. In recorded public hearings after the gap, Council voted 7-0 to approve a historic landmark designation, voted 0-7 (corrected from an initial 1-6 readout after Eugene Brown confirmed his intended no vote) to deny historic landmark designation for the Withall House (LDO 6-1) due to vinyl siding and replaced windows, and voted 7-0 to approve a voluntary annexation petition generating net positive cash flow. On pulled Consent Item 1 (2007 Legislative Program Outline), Council approved the overall package 7-0 while recording a 6-1 split vote on three items under the 'Other' category—Item 1 (local option transportation tax), Item 6 (homeowner impact fees), and Item 8 (prepared food/meals tax)—with Bill Bell, Cora Cole-McFadden, Howard Clement III, Mike Woodard, Eugene Brown, and Diane Catotti voting Aye and Thomas Stith III voting Nay. Before adjourning at 9:48 p.m., the City Manager also reported that HUD dismissed Section 3 minority hiring violation complaints by Vincent Brown and Harrison Enterprises regarding Eastway Village.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, Bill of Rights Defense Resolution, and Council Announcements
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bill Bell called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m., Council Member Howard Clement III led the Pledge of Allegiance, and roll call confirmed all seven seated members present. Council Member Mike Woodard read and presented a ceremonial resolution reaffirming the City's October 20, 2003 Bill of Rights Defense Resolution to Joan Walsh and members of the Durham Bill of Rights Defense Committee. Following truncated mid-segment remarks, Council members reported on the National League of Cities workshop in Reno, school traffic safety efforts around Jordan High School with County Commissioner Ellen Reckhow, school board members, and NCDOT, a staff project groundbreaking, and Mayor Pro Tempore Cora Cole-McFadden's attendance at the Crest Street Council annual meeting and a Senior Center for Life event, plus notice of the December 20 work session.

agenda_items.title: Priority Items by the City Manager, City Attorney, and City Clerk
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager asked Council to refer Agenda Item 28 (Police Department Long-Range Master Facility Plan) back to administration based on work session discussions, and requested that Deputy Chief Hodge present Supplemental Item 44 (Durham Police Department Third Quarter 2006 Crime Report) after the consent agenda alongside Supplemental Item 43 (Resolution Memorializing Benjamin S. 'Ben' Ruffin). Council Member Mike Woodard asked whether public comment on the police facilities plan would still be heard that evening given citizens in attendance. Council voted 7-0 to approve the City Manager's priority items; the City Attorney had no items, and the City Clerk provided a brief update.

agenda_items.title: General Consent Agenda Overview and Item Pulls (Portion Truncated)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Mayor Bell read through the General Consent Agenda, pulling Item 1 (2007 Legislative Program Outline) for discussion and noting items including board appointments (Cable TV Advisory Board, Durham Housing Authority, RDU Airport Authority, Workforce Development Board, Durham Convention and Visitors Bureau), carryover budget amendment (Item 8), UDI Community Development Corporation construction loan (Item 9, on which the Mayor recused himself from speaking), grant project ordinances (Items 10 and 16), October 2006 Business Loan Report (Item 11), Sales and Service Training Center contract amendment (Item 12), Results-Based Accountability interlocal agreement (Item 14), major site plans (Items 15 and 35), and supplemental Items 43 and 44. Council Member Howard Clement III noted receiving a neighborhood letter on Item 15 before the transcript digest was truncated through 02:29:03.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Historic Landmark Designation (Prior Item)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Resuming after the truncated middle portion of the meeting, Council concluded a public hearing on a historic landmark designation, with remarks noting that designation makes property modifications more difficult by requiring a Certificate of Appropriateness from the Historic Preservation Commission. No members of the public spoke for or against the proposal, and Council closed the public hearing and approved the item 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Historic Landmark Designation — Withall House (LDO 6-1)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Planning staff reported that both staff and the Historic Preservation Commission (following its November 7, 2006 public hearing) recommended denial of historic landmark designation for the Withall House because past alterations—including full vinyl siding and replaced, non-historically framed operable windows—left very little original historic character, while designation would reduce city taxable value by roughly $70,000. Responding to Council Member Eugene Brown's procedural question, the City Attorney advised making a motion to approve and voting it down to defeat the request. After an initial 1-6 display, the Clerk clarified and recorded the final vote as failing 0-7 after Eugene Brown confirmed his intended no vote.

agenda_items.title: Public Hearing: Voluntary Annexation Petitions Received by December 1, 2005
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Staff presenter Julie Brennan presented the continuation of a public hearing opened at the prior meeting for a voluntary annexation petition covering a property assemblage (transcribed as the 'failed road assemblage property'). She reported that annexing the property would produce a net positive cash flow to the City. No members of the public spoke, and Council closed the hearing and approved the annexation 7-0.

agenda_items.title: Pulled Consent Item 1: 2007 Legislative Program Outline
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Council took up pulled Item 1, with Council Member Howard Clement III confirming where a General Assembly item appeared in the revised handout (new General Item 8) and Council Member Diane Catotti offering comments. Public speakers included Cheryl Smith, who asked about the Second Chance program for youth seeking GEDs and jobs, and a speaker (following truncated remarks) opposing a proposed prepared food/meals tax unless funds were appropriately directed. Council Member Thomas Stith III asked to be recorded as voting no on three items under the 'Other' category—Item 1 (local option transportation tax), Item 6 (impact fees passed on to homeowners), and Item 8 (prepared food tax)—without severing them; Council approved the overall package 7-0 with Stith recorded as no on those three items (6-1).

agenda_items.title: City Manager Report: HUD Dismissal of Eastway Village Section 3 Complaint & Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The City Manager informed Council that the City had received a letter from the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD) dismissing Section 3 minority hiring violation claims brought by Vincent Brown and Harrison Enterprises regarding the Eastway Village project, noting a 15-day appeal window and promising copies for Council boxes the next day. Council then adjourned at 9:48 p.m. on a motion by Council Member Eugene Brown.

votes.discussion_detail: Following City Attorney guidance on a motion to approve so Council could defeat the request per staff and Historic Preservation Commission recommendations, Council voted down the designation due to non-historic vinyl siding and replaced windows.

votes.discussion_detail: Approved the 2007 Legislative Program Outline after discussion with Council members and public speakers.

votes.item_title: Item 1: 2007 Legislative Program Outline — 'Other' Category Items 1 (Transportation Tax), 6 (Impact Fees), and 8 (Prepared Food Tax)
votes.notes: Recorded in the combined vote on the 2007 Legislative Program Outline at 02:47:42 ('with Councilmember Stith voting no on item[s] under the Other: 1, 6, and 8').
votes.discussion_detail: Thomas Stith III opposed three revenue/tax proposals under the 'Other' category of the 2007 Legislative Program Outline—local option transportation tax (Item 1), impact fees passed on to homeowners (Item 6), and a prepared food/meals tax (Item 8)—and asked to be recorded as voting No on those three items without severing them.

disagreements.issue: 2007 Legislative Program Outline — Local Option Transportation Tax, Impact Fees, and Prepared Food Tax ('Other' Items 1, 6, and 8)
disagreements.summary: During consideration of the 2007 Legislative Program Outline, Council Member Thomas Stith III objected to three local revenue and tax proposals in the 'Other' category—a local option transportation tax (Item 1), homeowner impact fees (Item 6), and a prepared food/meals tax (Item 8)—while the remaining six Council members supported including them in the City's legislative package.
disagreements.side_a_position: Include the local option transportation tax, impact fees, and prepared food tax in the 2007 Legislative Program Outline.
side_a_arguments: Maintains the full legislative package to seek General Assembly authority for local revenue options, with clarification that Item 8 applies to prepared food and statements noted by a speaker that Council Member Diane Catotti indicated some proceeds would support workforce initiatives.
disagreements.side_b_position: Oppose including Other Items 1 (transportation tax), 6 (impact fees), and 8 (prepared food tax) in the legislative program.
side_b_arguments: Opposed raising the local option tax for transportation.
Argued impact fees would be passed on to homeowners.
Criticized the food/prepared food tax as a regressive tax.
disagreements.resolution: Council voted 7-0 on the overall 2007 Legislative Program Outline while recording Thomas Stith III as voting Nay on 'Other' Items 1, 6, and 8 (passing those three items 6-1).
